{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Inspect the revenue column
print("First few values of revenue:")
print(sales['revenue'].head(10))

# Check for thousands separators
print("\nUnique values in revenue with more than 1 digit:")
print(sales['revenue'].unique()[:10])  # Show first 10 unique values

# Check for the presence of commas
has_commas = sales['revenue'].str.contains(',', na=False)
print(f"\nRows with commas in revenue: {has_commas.sum()}")

# Check if any revenue is '999999.99' (QA orders)
qa_orders = sales[sales['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"\nNumber of QA orders (revenue = 999999.99): {len(qa_orders)}")

# Check for refunded orders
refunded_orders = sales[sales['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f"\nNumber of refunded orders: {len(refunded_orders)}")

# Check for valid revenue values
valid_revenue = sales[~sales['revenue'].isin(['999999.99', ''])]
print(f"\nNumber of valid revenue entries (excluding QA & empty): {len(valid_revenue)}")

# Now parse revenue: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_float'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Filter out QA orders and refunded orders
clean_sales = sales[(sales['revenue'] != '999999.99') & (sales['status'] == 'completed')]

# Now calculate total revenue per channel
revenue_by_channel = clean_sales.groupby('channel')['revenue_float'].sum()

# Print result
print("\nTotal revenue by channel (after cleaning):")
print(revenue_by_channel)"}
